text:
pagerduty: ALERT: node-nv-03 disk pressure detected (ephemeral at 98%). Kernel eviction pressure triggered. Affected pods: inference-gpu-prod-*, modelcache-host. Automatic eviction started. Page: @kiran oncall

kiran: saw it, acknowledging. grabbing logs now. which customers hit this?

sofia: noticed 5xx spike on /v1/generate for several customers around 09:12. latency up ~3-5x. three high-volume clients seeing errors. no alerts from RBAC yet.

mike: node-nv-03 shows /var/lib/redwood/modelcache at 92% used, logs under /var/log/redwood have runaway write. suspect old debug traces not rotated. pods evicted: inference-gpu-prod-12, inference-gpu-prod-13, modelcache-host-0. some pods restarted and then crashed with CUDA errors.

ops-lead: set INCIDENT_SEV=SEV2. notify CS to prep messaging. @customer-success please stand by. :rotating_light:

storage-sre: attaching kubelet logs snippet:
```
May 21 09:11:34 node-nv-03 kubelet[1234]: eviction manager: attempting to reclaim ephemeral-storage
May 21 09:11:34 node-nv-03 kernel: device sda1: writeback failed, journal bloat
May 21 09:12:01 inference-gpu-prod-12[pid]: modelcache: open() failed: ENOSPC
May 21 09:12:10 inference-gpu-prod-12[pid]: ERROR: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS at inference.cc:412
```

kiran: ok plan: 1) cordon node-nv-03 2) drain safely (delete-local-data) 3) restart modelcache on other nodes 4) clean logs and rotate 5) scale up spare pool to absorb load. anyone object?

mike: agree. doing cordon+drain now: `kubectl cordon node-nv-03 && kubectl drain node-nv-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`

infra-bot: Deploybot: started graceful eviction of pods on node-nv-03 at 09:14 UTC.

kiran: some pods stuck Terminating due to mounts not detaching. running `kubectl describe pod inference-gpu-prod-12` shows volume detachment timeout.

storage-sre: i'm on a shell on node-nv-03. journal shows heavy log write from modelcache GC loop. listing large files:
```
# ls -lh /var/log/redwood | sort -k5 -h
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 8.1G modelcache-debug.log
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 2.5G inference.log
```

storage-sre: safe cleanup: rotate and truncate debug log, keep last 100MB. `truncate -s 100M /var/log/redwood/modelcache-debug.log` then `systemctl restart rsyslog`

kiran: truncation done. freed ~8GB. node disk now at 55%. proceeding with drain again.

sofia: customer impact update: affected customers see 5xx -> fallback to cached responses for some routes, but real-time inference failing. CS prepping email: "Intermittent 5xx and increased latency on inference — mitigation in progress."

mike: after restart of modelcache-host on node-nv-05, I see workers come up but some show segfaults in logs:
```
[09:20:05] model-worker[pid]: segfault at 0x7fffa... ip 0x55a1e0
[09:20:06] model-worker[pid]: CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_OUT_OF_RESOURCES
```

kiran: segfault + cuda errors look like corrupted cached shards after unclean eviction. storage-sre: can we remount modelcache and run repair script?

storage-sre: running repair: `/opt/redwood/bin/modelcache_repair --scan --fix` on node-nv-05. will take ~2m per shard. doing one shard at a time to avoid further OOMs.

ops-lead: temporary mitigation: increase inference pool by provisioning 2 extra spare GPUs in dedicated pool and route traffic there. mike, please trigger scale-up.

mike: provisioning now: `rctl dedicated scale --pool inference-prod --add 2` — estimated 4m to be available. routing policy updated to prefer spare pool for new requests.

sofia: monitoring: errors drop after routing change but still 1-2% errors for long requests (likely in-progress requests that retried). CS sent preliminary note to impacted customers. positive reaction so far.

kiran: performed rolling restart of inference pods to pick up repaired shards. watch logs for CUDA errors.

infra-bot: Alert: node-nv-03 has flapped (Rebooted) during drain window at 09:28. Some kubelets re-registered, kube-proxy recreated.

mike: that's why some Terminating pods stuck — node rebooted mid-detach. fixed by force-deleting stuck pods: `kubectl delete pod inference-gpu-prod-12 --force --grace-period=0` then recreated on healthy nodes.

storage-sre: modelcache_repair completed for 6/8 shards on n5 nodes, residual corrupted files moved to /var/lib/redwood/modelcache/quarantine. leaving quarantine for postmortem.

kiran: summary so far: disk bloat (large debug log) triggered eviction on node-nv-03 -> pods evicted/restarted -> some modelcache shards corrupted -> CUDA segfaults/out_of_resources on restarted pods -> scaled spare pool and repaired shards -> errors reduced to baseline.

ops-lead: handoff: @mike will take night-oncall for follow-up and patch. next steps documented below.

mike: taking over. immediate TODOs: 1) remove debug logging in modelcache (PR queued) 2) add logrotate policy + cron for /var/log/redwood 3) add pre-eviction hook to gracefully flush modelcache KV 4) investigate why GC loop produced multi-GB debug log.

customer-success: sent customer update at 09:45: "We've mitigated an outage affecting inference generation for a subset of customers. Root cause is disk space pressure leading to pod evictions. We're continuing repairs and will follow up with RCA."

kiran: tagging this incident: disk-pressure -> log-bloat -> eviction -> modelcache corruption -> CUDA OOM/crash. recording metrics for postmortem. handing to night oncall @mike at 10:00 UTC.

oncall: acked, will continue monitoring metrics and start a short postmortem doc. please add any logs to the incident ticket. :white_check_mark:

ops-lead: closing pagerduty page for now. keep incident slack thread open for follow-up action items. :lock:
